dedupe_keys.name: swiss data cube analysis ready earth observation data for switzerland

description: The Swiss Data Cube (SDC) is an Earth observation data cube for Switzerland built by UN Environment GRID-Geneva and the University of Geneva, following the Open Data Cube approach of Geoscience Australia. Its aim is to support the Swiss government in environmental monitoring and reporting and to help Swiss research institutions use satellite data. It organises open and free analysis-ready data from Landsat (USGS), Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-1 (ESA), with Sentinel-3 and Sentinel-5P announced; the about page says that since 2018 all Landsat, Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 data are available for the whole country, after a first phase with 5 years of Landsat data and a second adding more than 30 years. The datasets are processed regularly and made available through the SDC platform, with products, a GeoServer, a viewer, an Atlas of Changing Switzerland and geoembeddings of Switzerland, and the team publishes studies such as snow detection and 35 years of vegetation greenness. The data is described as open and free; no licence is named on the pages read. Caveats: some news items are years old, and the platform is aimed at scientific and government users. Coverage is Switzerland. It supports hazard exposure and climate adaptation analysis, such as snow, drought and land change around Alpine roads, railways and hydropower; related records are Digital Earth Australia and Terrascope.
